subject: Question on annotation with genomic features and regional analysis

messages.author: 67571e909b2d8a9a
messages.subject: Question on annotation with genomic features and regional analysis
parts:
Hi,
 
Could I please get advise on the following or be directed to a relevant post if these issues have been previously raised.
 
First, how do I annotate a list of differential methylated cytosine (DMCs) with genonic features (i.e. intron, exon, promoter, intergenic)? I tried using the function annotate.WithGenicParts() which produced stats on the genomic features. However, I would like to link coordinates of  DMCs to the genomic feature (e.g. <chr><start><end><genomic_feature>) and not just getting information on the stats.
 
Second, regarding regional analysis, I wanted to confirm that regionCounts() should only be used on methylRaw or methylRawList object but not on methylBase objects.
 
Thanks.

You can stitch together the data from the methyDiff object and the 'members' slot of the annotationByGenicParts object with the cbind command. If you have for example named the objects, myDiffMeth and diffAnn, you can do the following:

I'm not too familiar with the region counts function, but the documentation indicates that it can be used with a methylBase object. If you need a way to generate the regions, you can use the Mason lab's eDMR package.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Question on annotation with genomic features and regional analysis
parts: First, how do I annotate a list of differential methylated cytosine (DMCs) with genonic features (i.e. intron, exon, promoter, intergenic)? I tried using the function annotate.WithGenicParts() which produced stats on the genomic features. However, I would like to link coordinates of  DMCs to the genomic feature (e.g. <chr><start><end><genomic_feature>) and not just getting information on the stats.

There is no function to do that, you just get a matrix at best showing if your DMC/DMR overlaps with exons/introns etc. But you can use findOverlaps() from GenomicRanges to get a matrix of indeces which can be used to arrive at genomic feature location to DMR/DMC mappings.
Second, regarding regional analysis, I wanted to confirm that regionCounts() should only be used on methylRaw or methylRawList object but not on methylBase objects.
regionCounts() can be used with methylBase objects, but there with default settings you will only count bases that are covered in all samples in your regions.

Thanks.

--

Last note- if you want the feature name (i.e. the RefSeq ID), you can use the dist,to.TSS slot. Putting that together with the members slot gives:

> head(cbind(getData(myDiffMeth),diffAnn@members, dif...@dist.to.TSS ))
